clue.text: Fellow needs month touring unknown country

indicators.note: to tour a place is to travel all around it, so the first pieces go round the unknown

parts.note: a fellow is a man
MAR is the short form of March
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: A man needs a month to travel around some unfamiliar land.
explanation.walkthrough: Unknown stands for an algebra letter here, and the touring pieces wrap round it just after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Myanmar, formerly Burma, is a nation in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Note king having trouble with emperor

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A musical king runs into difficulty over an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikado was the title formerly used abroad for the Japanese ruler, as in Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta.

clue.text: Condition in maths worked out attracting top grade

indicators.note: something attracting another draws it close, so an extra letter joins on

parts.note: A is the highest exam grade

indicators.note: a sum that is worked out is reworked step by step, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pupil's maths homework, once done, earns the best mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a chronic respiratory illness, a medical condition affecting breathing.

clue.text: Sauce from Irish county girl raised in north-east

parts.note: County Mayo is in the west of Ireland

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation

indicators.note: in a down clue something raised is read from bottom to top, so the name runs backwards

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A dressing comes from an Irish county, made by a girl brought up in the north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a thick cold dressing of egg yolk and oil.

clue.text: Bird losing wing and crest

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the whole

parts.note: a partridge is a game bird
a wing of a building is a part of it

explanation.surface: A bird has lost a wing and its crest of feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing' looks like one end of the bird, but it stands for PART, a section of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the crest of a hill or the top line of a roof.

clue.text: Ring for captain to supply troop with weapons?

parts.note: to arm is to supply with arms
a band is a troop or group
surface padding completing the sense of supply: to arm is to equip with weapons

explanation.surface: A captain asks whether to equip a troop with weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with weapons' completes the sense of ARM: to arm is to supply with weapons, and the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A team captain wears a band of cloth round the upper arm as a mark of the role.

clue.text: Instrument's first-rate hoist absorbing doubled force

indicators.note: something absorbing another takes it inside itself

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 read as I
F is force in physics; doubled gives two
a davit is a small crane on a ship for hoisting boats

explanation.surface: A musical instrument's excellent lifting gear takes in twice the force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests music, but it is a legal document; A1 holds FF between its two characters.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an instrument is a formal written document, and an affidavit is a sworn written statement.

clue.text: Donnybrook's rich source

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to the setter, Donnybrook, speaking in his own voice
second meaning: a plentiful supply, like a pit dug for ore

explanation.walkthrough: Donnybrook is this puzzle's setter, so his possession is what he would call his own.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for the speaker, and also a pit yielding coal or gold, figuratively an abundant store.

clue.text: A club with rising revelry? It might make a killing

parts.note: taken as written
a bat is a club used in sport

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upward, so that word runs backwards

parts.note: a riot is noisy revelry

explanation.surface: A club with growing merriment might be a moneymaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a killing' usually means profit hugely; here it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is where animals are killed, so it literally makes a killing.

clue.text: Set off from school in time

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a date is a time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone leaves school on time.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to set it off, triggering the explosion.

clue.text: Perhaps a small Abyssinian pot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a young cat, the Abyssinian being one breed
second meaning: the pool of money staked in a game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Abyssinian' suggests an Ethiopian, but it is a breed of cat; 'Perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is affectionately a kitty, and the shared fund of stakes in poker is also called that.

clue.text: One charged expert to pen last article

indicators.note: to pen something is to shut it in, like animals in an enclosure

parts.note: deft means skilful, expert
the last part is the end
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An accused person hires an expert to write the final article.
explanation.definitionFit: In court the person accused of a crime is the defendant, the one facing the charge.

clue.text: Stupid slur reportedly losing force

parts.note: dim means slow-witted

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so this is about sound

parts.note: an innuendo is an indirect slur

explanation.surface: A dim-witted insult loses its punch when it is passed on.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound of INNUENDO is spelt here with a single N.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a diminuendo is a gradual decrease in loudness, so the sound loses power.

clue.text: Bowl over, taking wicket ultimately in fine weather

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside
marks the outer word the letter goes inside

parts.note: sun is fine weather

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of wicket

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowls someone over and takes a wicket in sunny conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words are decoration: 'Bowl over' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is to astonish or amaze them, as does stunning them.

clue.text: Morgan dead, butchered in final battle

indicators.note: something butchered is hacked about and mangled into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Morgan is found slaughtered during the last fight.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Revelation, Armageddon is the site of the last conflict between good and evil.

clue.text: Pass duke with rapid progress

parts.note: to hand over is to pass
dukes is old slang for fists

explanation.surface: A duke walks through, making swift headway.
explanation.walkthrough: Dukes, as in 'put up your dukes', is slang for fists.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is used for making money or gaining ground very quickly.

clue.text: Energy to limit velocity when rocketing in void

indicators.note: in a down clue something rocketing shoots upward, so the string reads bottom to top

parts.note: E is the physics symbol
to cap is to limit
velocity is speed

explanation.surface: Fuel is used to cap a rocket's speed as it climbs into emptiness.
explanation.definitionFit: The far reaches beyond our planet's atmosphere are the vast emptiness of the cosmos.

clue.text: Photograph cracks

parts.note: a snap is a crack, a sharp breaking sound
a shot is a crack of a gun, or a try

explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'cracks' supplies two separate words, each a kind of crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick informal picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Fruit centre in pod crane ripped apart

indicators.note: something ripped apart is torn to bits and the pieces reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A seed pod is torn up by a crane.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists call the innermost layer of a fruit's wall, such as a stone around the seed, the endocarp.

clue.text: Sonnet line as revised becomes dispensable

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet decides that a line of a sonnet can be cut when the draft is edited.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnecessary can be done without, so it is not required.

clue.text: Beat time welcoming Rugby School skipper

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
T is the abbreviation for time
RU stands for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: Someone beats the clock to greet the captain of Rugby School.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby School is a famous English private school, but here the words split: Rugby gives RU, and 'School skipper' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant is a pupil who stays away from lessons without permission, skipping classes.

clue.text: Mate's going north, skirting constant danger to shipping

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means travelling upward, so the word reads backwards
to skirt something is to go round its edge

parts.note: a mate is an ally, with the possessive S
c is the constant for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A ship's mate sails north, steering around a persistent hazard at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Scylla was the sea monster opposite Charybdis that seized sailors from passing vessels.

clue.text: Specialist brought to western front

parts.note: a pro is a professional, a specialist
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: An expert is sent to the Western Front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western front' reads as the First World War line, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: The prow is the forward part of a ship's bow.

clue.text: Unbalanced May's contrived measuring system

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the metric system of measures

explanation.surface: Theresa May's plan for weights and measures is lopsided and artificial.
explanation.definitionFit: Asymmetric shapes lack matching halves, so their sides are not in balance.

clue.text: Legendary king married princess to son

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married
Princess Ida is the heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A mythical king marries a princess off to his son.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Midas was the Phrygian ruler whose touch turned everything to gold.

clue.text: German managed, escaping Walpole's castle

indicators.note: what is escaping gets out and is gone, so it is removed

parts.note: Horace Walpole wrote the Gothic novel The Castle of Otranto
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A German got away from Walpole's castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Horace Walpole's 1764 novel The Castle of Otranto began the Gothic genre; RAN comes out of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a typical German man's name, borne by Bismarck and several emperors.

clue.text: Catch tense boy round new central zone

indicators.note: going round something encloses it

parts.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it
T is a grammar abbreviation for tense
a lad is a boy
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A nervous boy is caught near a new middle area.
explanation.definitionFit: The heartland is the core region of a country or activity, its middle area.

clue.text: Create image with line in slow speech

parts.note: to draw is to create a picture
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a picture, with a line, while talking slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a lazy manner of talking with drawn-out vowels.

clue.text: Excellent work secured by pin

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast inside it

parts.note: a thole is a peg on a boat's side that holds an oar
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A fine piece of handiwork is fastened with a pin.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-hole is dated British upper-class slang for first-class or splendid.

clue.text: Entertainer among travellers in a train

indicators.note: among says the letters sit in the middle of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of travellers through the start of train

explanation.surface: A performer sits with other passengers on a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the American singer and actor, a famous performer of the twentieth century.
